name: relative-size-discrimination
title: Catch the Larger, Avoid the Smaller
question:
Does the evolved agent catch the second object when it is larger than the
first and avoid it when smaller — above what any memoryless policy can do?
claim:
The agent categorizes by RELATIVE size, reaching 0.688 accuracy (catch 0.625,
avoid 0.75) — above the 0.625 ceiling that any single-object (memoryless)
policy can reach on this role-balanced battery, and above the 0.5 always-catch
/ always-avoid baselines.

expected_behavior.name: categorizes-above-memoryless-ceiling
expected_behavior.rationale:
Accuracy > 0.625 (the best any absolute-size threshold reaches here) AND >
0.5 (always-catch/always-avoid), on BOTH relations (catch and avoid each >
0.5). Verified in tests/test_relational_seed.py. Beating the memoryless
ceiling requires using object 1 relative to object 2 — i.e. memory.

findings.summary: Accuracy 0.688 (catch 0.625, avoid 0.75) — above the 0.625 memoryless ceiling and the 0.5 fixed-policy baselines; a genuine but imperfect relational categorizer.
findings.detail:
figures/relational.gif shows a should-catch and a should-avoid trial and the
outcome; figures/decision_map.png shows the learned response over the (s1,s2)
plane tracking the s2=s1 diagonal (imperfectly).
